column1: # EN-21. What the ZAP baseline does with each rule, one rule per line:
#   <rule id><TAB><IGNORE|INFO|WARN|FAIL><TAB><what it is, and for IGNORE why>
# Threshold: the build FAILS only on the rules marked FAIL below. Those are checks the web app and the
# API pass today, so a change that breaks one is a regression and is stopped. Everything else WARNs:
# it is reported (job summary, zap-report artifact) and does not fail the build, because the first scan
# found Medium and Low items that need a decision from the people who own the headers and the API
# (documentation/evidence/EN-21/zap.md lists each). A rule is IGNOREd only with its reason on the line.
# The scan is unauthenticated and passive; it never attacks.
# Regression guards: clean on both targets in the first scan.

column3: Server leaks its version in the Server header
Application error disclosure (stack traces and the like in a response)

Storable and Cacheable Content (informational). The web assets are fingerprinted files that are meant to be cached for a year and index.html is no-cache; the API response flagged is the 404 for a path that does not exist. An unauthenticated scan sees no user data, so there is nothing sensitive to be cached.
Timestamp Disclosure - Unix (low). The one hit is a constant inside a bundled third-party library (1540483477, in 2018), not a server clock or user data.
Modern Web Application (informational). Says the spider cannot see client-side routes; that is a known limit of this scan, written down in documentation/evidence/EN-21/zap.md, not a weakness.
